dedupe_keys.name: spatial accessibility of hospital services in italy municipality and hospital data for a gravity model hip replacement

description: This data set supports a study of whether people in Italy have fair geographic access to hospital care for hip replacement, and whether poor access pushes them to travel to hospitals in other regions. The producer is Fabrizio Pecoraro of the Institute for Research on Population and Social Policies at Italy's National Research Council. Coverage is all Italian municipalities, using 2011 boundaries, and the hospitals that perform the procedure; the second version limits the population to residents aged 55 or over. Files give municipality and hospital attributes, a distance matrix between every municipality and hospital, aggregated inputs for a gravity-type accessibility measure that splits access within and across regions, and the municipal boundary shapefile. The data are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the deposit has little documentation of column meanings and data years, which are explained in the associated article, and it covers one elective procedure. Simulation uses: modelling patient flows between regions, testing how closing or expanding hospital capacity changes access and mobility, and building gravity models of hospital choice. Related records: the Italian hospital bed data by structure (data-italy-hospital-beds-by-structure-2010-2017) come from the same author, and the Spanish accessibility data (data-spain-hospital-accessibility-census-tracts) give a comparable measure.
